title: Roman questions about free choice touched only so far as they bear on present controversies
source_text: I. De Liberi Arbitrii natura & essentia multas quaestiones movent, & inter se agitant Doctores Scholae Romanae; quae tamen potius ad Metaphysicos, quam ad Theologos pertinent: neque omnes hic recensere & excutere est animus; sed ea solum breviter attingere quae aliquo modo spectant ad eas controversias quibus hodie fervent, & super quibus inter se digladiantur Scholae Christianae.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the nature and essence of free Choice the Doctors of the Roman School raise and agitate among themselves many questions; which however pertain rather to Metaphysicians than to Theologians: nor is it my purpose to review and examine them all here; but only briefly to touch those which in some way look to those controversies with which the Christian Schools are today on fire, and over which they fight among themselves.
pass_b_english: The teachers of the Roman School debate many questions among themselves about what free choice is and what makes it what it is. Most of these belong more to metaphysics than to theology, and there is no intention here of listing and sifting them all.
Only those will be touched, and briefly, that bear somehow on the controversies now inflaming the Christian schools and dividing them against one another.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
